LESSON: READING 10.2.1 INTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.2: Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading, part of Strand 10 in Grade 5 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why do we read books? 2. Why should we make notes when reading? 3. What makes you a good reader?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. skim through a text and obtain the main idea,

2. scan through a text to obtain specific information,

3. discuss and relate ideas to their experiences collaboratively with peers,

4. read a text independently and retell it in own words,

5. answer direct and inferential questions from the text,

6. watch a video on leisure time and write the main points. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. skim through a text and obtain the main idea,
2. scan through a text to obtain specific information,
3. discuss and relate ideas to their experiences collaboratively with peers,
4. read a text independently and retell it in own words,
5. answer direct and inferential questions from the text,
6. watch a video on leisure time and write the main points. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to Learn is enhanced as the learner uses skimming and scanning skills to obtain information from a text.

• Self-efficacy is developed as the learner scans through a text to obtain specific information.

Values:
Responsibility is inculcated as the learner reads different texts and retells the stories in their own words independently.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Safety and Security: Personal safety is nurtured as the learner acquires reading skills and uses them on proper

utilisation of leisure time to keep themselves safe from environmental dangers.

Link to other Learning Areas

The learner applies the skill of intensive reading to Kiswahili where such a skill is emphasised.
